Furthermore, the rise of digital communication has fundamentally altered how communities maintain cultural boundaries and transmit intergenerational knowledge, challenging traditional anthropological understandings of cultural continuity and authenticity in the contemporary world.

prompt_inputs.content: Recent advances in CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing have demonstrated significant improvements in off-target mitigation through the implementation of high-fidelity SpCas9 variants, particularly eSpCas9 and SpCas9-HF1, which reduce unintended DNA cleavage by up to 90% compared to wild-type Cas9. Additionally, the development of base editing systems, including cytosine base editors (CBEs) and adenine base editors (ABEs), has enabled precise point mutations without generating double-strand breaks. These innovations have facilitated therapeutic applications in hemophilia A treatment and sickle cell disease, where ex vivo editing of patient-derived hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) combined with lentiviral vector integration has shown promising results in Phase I/II clinical trials. Furthermore, multiplexed CRISPR approaches utilizing dual sgRNA scaffolds have improved the efficiency of large chromosomal deletions for cancer immunotherapy, while emerging in vivo delivery mechanisms employing lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) and adeno-associated viruses (AAVs) continue to expand therapeutic possibilities.
